The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that took place on 24.06.2019.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 24.06.2019 at about 12.15 p.m., when he was proceeding in the Honda Passion Pro motor cycle bearing Reg. 3. Immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Government hospital, Sira, thereafter shifted to KIMS hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment for the accidental injuries.
It is stated that the injured was an agriculturist and doing a coconut and areca nut tendering business and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is not able to do his work as he was doing earlier and lost his income.
It is stated that he has spent huge amount for his treatment, medicine etc.,
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the driver of the Offending bus bearing Reg. No. KA- 42-A-1984.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 3 rd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.2 has entered appearance through its learned counsel and filed objection statement.
Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 and 2 remained absent, hence they were placed exparte.
5. The 3rd respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.

This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending bus bearing Reg. No.
KA-42-A-1984 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy, valid driving license of the driver of the vehicles involved in the accident, the registration certificate,
fitness certificate and permit of the vehicle and the provision of the motor vehicles Act and Rules.
It has denied the age, occupation and income, period of hospitalization and treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is high exorbitant.
On other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-A- 1984?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?

It is specifically urged that, the accident occurred due th the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

11. In order to substantiate the contentions petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R, F.I.S, spot mahazar, IMV Report, wound certificate and charge sheet as per Ex.

12. The version of the petitioners remains unchallenged and undisputed.
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
13. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of bus.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:

sentences.text: Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

14. According to the version of petitioners the accident happened near Lakkavvanahalli Cross,
Dwarankunte Road, Gowdagere Hobli, Sira Taluk, Tumkur District, when the driver of bus came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle in which petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion after 9 days of accident as per Ex.P2.
Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2, the FIR registered by Pattanayakanahalli P.S. based on the first information given by one Hanumantharaya.
The first informant is given by the brother in law of the petitioner.
He gave first information to the police on 03.07.2019.
The alleged accident was occurred on 24.06.2019.
the first information was given after 9 days of the accident.

It is important to note that the priority is to be given to provide medical aid to the injured and not to lodge first information, moreover, all the family members might have rushed to the hospital when they heard about the accident to their family member.
The injured was discharged from the hospital on 28.07.2019.

Hence, there is a delay of nine days in lodging first information, but it cannot be doubted since soon after the accident the injured was admitted to the hospital and all the documents goes to show that the injured sustained injuries in road traffic accident.
15. The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence is Ex.P3 being the Spot Mahazar.

On close perusal of the Ex.P.3 it reflects that injured/petitioner was pillion rider on the motorcycle,
his motorcyclist was proceeding in his lane on the left side of the road and the width of the road is 18 feet.

Suddenly the offending bus came in a negligent manner from opposite direction and hit the Dodde Gowda .L vs Rajesh on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88085238/

The said factum is also fortified with the IMV report.
If the driver of bus had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle, then he would certainly avoid the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.4 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P6 is also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case, having regard to Ex.P.3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P.6 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the bus driver.

16. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.

19. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:

It is the case of the petitioner that prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was doing agriculture work and areca nut tendering business and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and to prove the same, petitioner has produced 3 RTCs' at Ex.P11 to 13 which stands in the name of petitioner, Also produced bills issued by Agriculture produce market at Ex.P14 to P28 which shows that petitioner was selling agricultural products to the market.
In the absence of document of income, the tribunal has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2019.
Considering the avocation and the year of the accident, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,000/- per month.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.
The petitioner got examined the Doctor as PW.3.

In the evidence of doctor, he has deposed that petitioner sustained injury to head, right upper limb and the CT scan of head shows the injuries of haemorrhagic contusions in left temporal right frontoparietal cortex, surrounding oedema, petechial haemorrhages in right fronto parietal and left occipital cortex,
subrachnpid haemorrhage, subdural haematoma in left quadrigeminal cistern and took treatment at KIMS hospital and research centre, Bengaluru.
He was treated conservatively.

On clinical examination conducted by him he found that petitioner is complains of memory loss, forgets things, names, conversations and difficult to identify and recognize people, gets angry easily, giddiness, gets irritated with loud noise/sounds,
difficulty in walking and speaking, needs support of others for walking and not able to do his works as before.
On examination, patient brought in wheel chair and he was able to walk with great difficultly with support of others.
Patient was conscious, obeys commands.
He has imbalance and needs support his higher mental functions are impaired, his memory is also impaired.

Petitioner fall under the category of moderately severe disability,
unable to attending to his own bodily needs without assistance, and unable to walk unassisted.
PW.3 has assessed 75% permanent physical impairment due to neurological conditions due to head injury.
In the cross examination PW.3 has denied the suggestion that petitioner has not sustained any loss of memory and speech and stated that there is problem in speech.
Further he has also produced wound certificate at Ex.P7 which reveals the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
The Ex.P8 Discharge Summary of KIMS Hospital reveals that petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 24.06.2019 to 28.07.2019 and took conservative treatment.

It could be borne out from cross examination that, petitioner can carryout his day- Dodde Gowda .L vs Rajesh on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88085238/
7 to-day activities with some difficulties and with the assistance.
The main complaint is that the petitioner has memory deficits and he face difficulties in making day to day decisions, reasoning and judgment.
At the same juncture this court will also does not loose sight on the fact that the assessment was done by the PW.3.
The petitioner has given evidence before the court on 07.03.2023 in his own capacity.
Further on perusal of cross examination he had given rational answers.
Further it could be culled out from the cross-examination of PW.1 that he has deposed before the court by glancing through his memory over the years.
When such being the case, beyond any stretch of imagination this court is not persuaded with the observation made by PW.3 with regard to the loss of memory from the petitioner.

The clarification with regard to loss of memory finds place in the cross-examination of PW.1 wherein he had given the rational answers and also denied many of the suggestions made by the respondent counsel.
When such being the case, this court cannot completely rely on the evidence of PW.3.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that the doctor has assessed the disability on higher side.

Further, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajaykumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows;
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.

This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

sentences.text: third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.
20. By applying the said precedent to the present case the petitioner is facing deficiency in mental speed, focused attention, verbal fluency.
Petitioner has also sustained other injuries.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 30%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 20%.
It is contended that petitioner was aged 50 years as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 24.06.2019.

However, by considering the birth year mentioned in Ex.P35 Adhaar card as 1965,
the petitioner was aged 54 years at the time of accident.
The multiplier applicable to the age of 54 is 11 as per the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation(AIR 2009 SC 3104).

22. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced medical bills to the tune of Rs.3,52,137/- as per Ex.P9,
medical prescriptions at Ex.P10.
I have examined the medical bills and receipts.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.3,52,137/- and he is entitled for the same.

23. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 34 days, and also took follow treatment as out patient.
Certainly he might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.35,000/- under this head.

24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.56,000/- (14,000 X 4) under this head.

25. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE/MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS:
The petitioner was aged about 54 years at the time accident and on account of accident, he has to suffer the above disability.
He has to suffer this discomfort and sacrifice the amenities through out his remaining life.

28. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-A-1984.
It is not in dispute that 1 st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 3rd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The 3rd respondent shall indemnify the 1 st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But mere unchallenged and undisputed facts does not amounts to proof of the same.
The petitioner is bestowed with the burden to prove the specific assertions in the light of oral and documentary proof.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
It is important to note that the priority is to be given to provide medical aid to the injured and not to lodge first information, moreover, all the family members might have rushed to the hospital when they heard about the accident to their family member.
The injured was discharged from the hospital on 28.07.2019.
Hence, there is a delay of nine days in lodging first information, but it cannot be doubted since soon after the accident the injured was admitted to the hospital and all the documents goes to show that the injured sustained injuries in road traffic accident.
If the driver of bus had come in a normal speed by observing ongoing vehicle, then he would certainly avoid the accident.
Added more the contents of Ex.P.4 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle.
Further more, even the chargesheet as per Ex.P6 is also filed as against the driver of the bus.
When such is the case, having regard to Ex.P.3 and 4 coupled with Ex.P.6 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving of the bus driver.
Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Even in the instant case the driver of the bus is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the bus and he was charge sheeted.
Further, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajaykumar and another, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows;
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so the extent of such permanent disability.
This means that the tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement,
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is the permanent disability suffered by the person.
In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.
Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity.
20. By applying the said precedent to the present case the petitioner is facing deficiency in mental speed, focused attention, verbal fluency.
Petitioner has also sustained other injuries.
When such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work effectively, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 30%, cannot be ruled out.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,69,600/-(Rs.14,000x12x11x20/100)
towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability.
24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.
